YAWNING, an involuntary opening of the mouth, occasioned by a vapour or ventosity endeavouring to escape, and generally witnessing an irksome weariness, or an in-, clination to deep. Yawning, according to Boerhaavc, is performed by expanding at one and the lame time all the muscles capable of spontaneous motion ; by greatly extending the lungs ; by drawing in gradually and dowlya large quantity of air ; and gradually and (lowly breathing it out, after it has been retained for some time, and rarified; and then restoring the muscles to their natural (late. Hence the effect of yawning is to move, accelerate, and equally distribute all the humours through all the vessels of the body, and consequently to qualify the muscles and organs of sensation for their various funds sons.

To these a person is most inclined just after deep, because, a greater quantity going off by the pores of the (kin than at other times, whensoever a person wakes, the increased contraction that then happens closes a great deal of the perspirable matter in the cutaneous passages, which -will continually give such irritations as excite yawning and stretching ; and such motions, by (baking the membranes of the whole body, and (hitting the contacts of their fibres, and the inclosed matter, by degrees throw it off. Hence we fee the reason why healthful strong people are most inclined to such motions, because they perspire most in time of deep, and therefore have more of the perspirable matter to lodge in the pores, and greater irritations thereunto.
